### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b09f5c2f244c926af3aaaa4205c65544f20a7b01` — the merge of head `1ddbf04f9744e4a77113e6103424809fdc27d216` into base `be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b09f5c2f244c926af3aaaa4205c65544f20a7b01 && git checkout b09f5c2f244c926af3aaaa4205c65544f20a7b01
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75 1ddbf04f9744e4a77113e6103424809fdc27d216 && git checkout -B drift-repro be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75 && git merge --no-ff 1ddbf04f9744e4a77113e6103424809fdc27d216

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs be75078a48c01519067c560e760fda09f156ea75` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48514584223504779868e69d796f71352b78f223`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-action-slots.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts + cited and read, never reviewed: packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/stored-envelope.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (the changeset .changeset/32352-action-removal-every-slot.md is read for ②)

PR #32533 for card #32352, net diff against `main` (merge base `e06d04f94`): 5 files, +263 / -20. Read: the card body and all six comments (triage 6780352504, amendment 6781609404, triage 6784724180, Claim 6812576869, seat ruling 6812619720, os-dev-report 6813526360), the PR body, the diff, and the check-runs on this head.

Gates on this head when read (their conclusions are the verdicts, none re-run):
- success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Plan Test Core shards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Auto Label, filter, Flag docs affected by code changes.
- still running, no verdict yet: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI.
- The pins' green is therefore NOT yet a gate verdict on this head: Test Core carries them. This record judges the design; landing waits for those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

The only code change is `storeRemovalKeys` plus the new private `refuseSeveralPackages` in `package-slotted-store.ts`. `metadata-manager.ts` changes a doc comment only. No export, signature or schema moves; `storeRemovalKeys` is not exported from the package index.

1. `unregister('action', x, { packageId: P })`: the registry keys are now every key of the name whose package is P (`storeKeysNamed` filtered by `slotPackageOf`), where it was the one object-less key. RIGHT: it is the card's Do 1 and the ruling's first bullet. The name's package-less slot is still never taken (its `slotPackageOf` is undefined), and another package's slot is never taken.
2. `unregister('action', x)` with two or more packages on any key of the name (same object, two objects, one bound and one object-less): refused 409 `ambiguous-in-environment`, `callerPackageId: null`, every package a candidate in store order, with the owners sentence when any slot is bound. RIGHT: the ruling's option A. It tightens and never loosens; it names every candidate; it does not pick.
3. The same call over `DatabaseLoader` rows (S7): `removalOf` already judged the registry and then the registry-plus-loaders view through the one rule, so the refusal now fires before step 1 of `unregisterAt`. RIGHT: read in `removalOf` and `slotViewOf`; the view keys loader items object-aware and the rule counts them by package, which equals the loader's `(package, name)` row count.
4. `MemoryLoader.delete('action', x)` called directly with no package (the class is a public export of `@objectstack/metadata`): it asks the same rule over object-aware keys, so for a name two packages bind it moved FROM deleting every slot TO throwing the 409. RIGHT as an answer (same rule, same arm), but it is a moved answer of a public door that the PR's table does not list and no pin calls directly. See ④ S1.
5. `DatabaseLoader.delete` called directly: its store is keyed by row key (`package`, `name`), so the old count and the new count are the same set, and the values are row arrays, for which `boundObjectOf` answers undefined, so the message is the old one byte for byte. UNCHANGED, right.
6. Other slotted types (`api`, `agent`, `skill`, `email_template`, `permission`): a key's identity is its name, so the package-named branch selects the one key it selected before, and the bare branch counts the same packages in the same store order with the same message. UNCHANGED, right.
7. Object-less-only action refusal: `anyBound` is false, message unchanged. RIGHT, pinned as CONTROL. Note the mixed case (two object-less holders plus a third package's bound slot) now names three candidates where it named two; that follows from judgment 2 and is right.
8. One package plus a package-less slot, and one package on several objects: one holder, not refused, every key of the name taken, as on `main`. UNCHANGED, right (the ruling counts packages; the second is pinned as CONTROL, the first is not pinned and did not move).
9. `unregisterPackage`: passes its own keys to `unregisterAt` and never asks the rule. UNCHANGED, right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, the BREAKING banner, the first-party count (0), a FROM → TO line with its one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no-migration-prescription). `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` conclude success on this head.

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` matches the diff: a call that was admitted is now refused. It is the arm the seat ruling required.
- The level follows the declared kind: `narrowed` takes `minor`. Whether the kind is `narrowed` or `none` is the dev's flag, answered in ③; either way `minor` is not below what the diff publishes.
- The changeset's account of the old behaviour was checked against `main`'s `storeRemovalKeys` and holds: the package-named branch returned the object-less key only, and the bare branch counted `packageSlotsOf(store, name)`, the object-less identity only.
- Nit: the changeset's one BREAKING line reads "a name two packages bind (one object or two)". The bullet above it also covers one bound and one object-less; the FROM → TO line should name that third shape too.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report 6813526360 carries `open_questions: []`. Its flags, each answered:

1. Declaration: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, moved from the Claim's provisional `none`, "the seat may rule it back". ANSWERED, accepted with a caveat. By the letter of the rule the kind is about what a metadata author can write, and a service removal that turns 409 is not authored metadata, which reads `none` (patch, banner kept). The dev cites the epic's ruling 6810963021 as precedent; that ruling is outside this review's inputs and was not read. `narrowed` with `minor` overstates at worst and the gate accepts it, so it does not block. ESCALATED to the seat only as a consistency call: confirm the precedent applies, or rule it back to `none`.
2. Deviation: no edit to `DatabaseLoader.delete` or `MemoryLoader.delete`. ANSWERED, accepted. Read in the cited code: the DB loader groups rows by `storeRowKey` and asks the rule, so its count is by package already; the memory loader's package-named branch already filtered by package. Ruling A needs no loader edit.
3. Deviation: no objectql edit. ANSWERED, accepted. The rule's only askers are `metadata-manager.ts`, `database-loader.ts` and `memory-loader.ts`; objectql keeps no removal slot.
4. Deviation and ruling condition 3: landing waits for PR #32497 and another merge of `main`. NOT MET at this head by the PR's own statement, and not checked here. ESCALATED to the seat as a landing condition: a merge of `main` produces a new head, and this record names this head only.
5. Out-of-scope finding, "noted, not filed, carrier: none": one package binding one action name to two objects keeps one `DatabaseLoader` row, the later save overwriting the earlier. ESCALATED. It is a stored-item loss that predates this card and is not made worse by it, but a finding with no carrier is lost. The seat files a card or records why none is owed.
6. Ruling condition 1 (three moved answers as FROM → TO with the census): present in the PR body. Ruling condition 2 (S7 pinned): present, see ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`** — holds against the code it cites and against the card, amendment S7 and ruling A. Attempts to break it:

- By-package removal of a bound action: keys are filtered by package over every key `storedNameOf` maps to the name, so the bound slot goes and the other package's stays. Holds.
- Bare removal, two packages, same object / different objects / one bound and one object-less: the holder map is built by package over all keys, size 2, refused, both named with their objects. Holds for all three.
- One package plus a package-less slot: the package-less key is skipped by the holder map, one holder, admitted, as on `main`. Holds, and agrees with the DB loader, which also counts packages only.
- S7: the manager's view is the registry's keys plus every loader's `loadSlots`; the DB loader reports one slot per row with the row's package, so the manager counts at least the packages the loader's own delete counts. Whenever the loader would refuse, the manager has refused first. Holds.
- Watcher and realtime events: a refusal throws inside `removalOf`, before any loader delete, registry delete or publish. Holds.
- `unregisterPackage`: untouched, does not ask the rule. Holds.

Findings:

- **S1, should-fix.** `MemoryLoader.delete` with no package is a public door of the same rule (derived judgment 4). Its answer for a name two packages bind moved from "deletes every slot" to "throws the 409". The PR's prose says the door's `MemoryLoader` asks the rule, but the moved-answers table lists `unregister` only, and no pin calls `door.delete('action', name)` directly: in the match-endpoint pins the manager refuses before the door is reached, so the door's own refusal is never exercised. The epic asks every moved answer to be declared and pinned. Not graded must-fix because the answer is the ruled one under the arm already declared, nothing first-party calls a loader's `delete` except the manager, and the manager cannot reach it in this state. Owed: one table row (or row 2 widened to name the loader door) and one direct pin.
- **N1, nit.** The rule's doc says "the refusal names each package with the object it binds the name to". Over `DatabaseLoader`'s row store the values are row arrays, so its own direct refusal names the packages and no objects. Every candidate is still named, and through the manager the objects are named. The doc should say the object sentence is the in-memory stores' and the manager's.
- **N2, nit.** The module header still says "The D3 refusal fires only among slots of one identity"; for a removal that is no longer so. The header's **remove** bullet also still says "that package's slot only". Both are prose in the same file as the changed rule.

**`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`** — doc-only hunk on `removalOf`. The new sentence is true of the code: the second `storeRemovalKeys` call over `slotViewOf` is what refuses S7. One limit of the surviving sentence "a loader the removal deletes from does not refuse once it has passed", read in code outside the diff and not graded against it:

- **N3, nit.** The agreement is between the manager's view (`loadSlots`, which reads the type-wide cached rows and skips a row whose body cannot be parsed) and the loader's delete (`rowSlots`, a fresh read that keeps such a row when its `package_id` column is set). A corrupt row or a stale type cache can still let the manager pass while the loader refuses, and a loader delete that throws for any other reason is still logged, the registry cleared and `deleted` announced. Both predate this card. The ruling's condition 2 is read as the S7 scenario, which is closed; the general "a delete that throws" policy is not this card's and is named here so it is not mistaken for closed.

**Tests** — read to judge whether the pins pin the declared FROM → TO:

- Row 1 (fix): pinned in both files; `get(..., ALPHA)` undefined, `list` holds only the other package, door and row gone for A and kept for B, the realtime event names A. These would be red on `main`'s rule. Real pins.
- Row 2 (narrowing): three shapes pinned at the registry with code, status, reason, `callerPackageId`, exact candidates, the object sentence, and "nothing removed". Real pins.
- Row 3 (S7): three shapes over a real `DatabaseLoader` on the file's row driver plus the door; they assert the refusal, registry, door and rows kept, no realtime event, no watcher event and no error logged. This is the ruling's condition 2. Real pins.
- CONTROLs: object-less two-holder message, one package on two objects, one package's bound action over the DB. They hold the unchanged answers.
- Gap, part of S1: no direct pin of the `MemoryLoader` door's own refusal. Not pinned and not moved: one package plus a package-less slot.
- The ablation the PR reports (10 red, 3 CONTROLs green) is the dev's account and was not re-run; the reading above agrees with it.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), three nits, one changeset nit.
